summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and, per the 2013-2014 National Register nomination and Historic Preservation Commission plan, still housed BAE Systems' electrical service shortly before rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown. The state's Office of Historic Preservation lists the 'Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation' of the '20th Street Historic Buildings at Pier 70' among its 2023 Governor's Historic Preservation Awards; its statement does not name individual buildings, but the Historic Preservation Commission's 2013 packet includes this building in that group.

milestones.text: Built for Bethlehem Steel as Powerhouse No. 1 of the Union Iron Works shipyard, to Charles Peter Weeks's design; equipment dating from 1913-1914 remained in 2013
Port Commission endorses the Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (Resolution 10-27), which calls for a National Register district and rehabilitation of the 20th Street buildings

Port Commission awards the 20th Street Historic Buildings opportunity to Orton Development after a 2011 RFP; Exclusive Negotiating Agreement approved April 2012; term sheet endorsed October 2012 (Board of Supervisors December 2012)

Historic Preservation Commission informational packet (memo dated Nov 26, 2013; the hearing date is not stated in the packet) on the rehabilitation of the ten 20th Street Historic Buildings (case 2013.1168E): ~270,000 gsf existing plus ~69,000 gsf of new mezzanines, ~334,000 gsf total
Union Iron Works Historic District listed in the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 14000150), giving the project access to federal historic tax credits
Port Commission Resolution 14-33 approves the Lease Disposition and Development Agreement and 66-year Master Lease (L-15814) with Historic Pier 70, LLC (Orton) and adopts CEQA findings

Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed, giving Orton site control; the Port's January 2019 memo says construction commenced thereafter. The National Trust (Winter 2016 issue) says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' without printing the year, which would be September 2015, while Bisnow (April 2017) says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'; the sources do not agree on the start year
Permanent financing for the Historic Core project achieved

Port staff update to the Commission (memo dated Jan 4, 2019): six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; whole-Historic-Core project total costs (not the cost of this building alone) rose from $81.9M at 2014 approvals to $127.0M in Table 2's '2018, Actual' column, while the memo's text gives 'an estimated $125 million at project completion in 2020'; Table 2 marks one line (Building 102's $6.7M) as a future-expenditure estimate
Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award
2013 plan: ODI to redevelop the 11,266 sq ft former Compressor House as a restaurant with an exterior dining deck, after the Port removes BAE's electrical facilities

Building abated of PCB electrical equipment; new shipyard electrical service occupies part of the basement; rehabilitation of the remainder under way with completion anticipated in 2019; public disappointment noted that it will be office, not a restaurant

Port Commission meeting on JUUL Labs' ten-year sublease of Building 102: attendees ask whether the City can evict JUUL; per Potrero View (Mar 2019), commissioners want to shorten the lease or pass an ordinance, but the Port Director says the Port's hands are tied and the City Attorney is examining JUUL's compliance
Port's January 2019 update lists completing the Building 102 rehabilitation and tenant improvements among its 2019 remaining milestones (a schedule item, not a confirmation that it was finished)

Rehabilitation profiled: seismic bracing, mezzanine, 2,600 sq ft rear addition with rooftop deck, one of four historic compressors retained; Marcy Wong Donn Logan wins a Metamorphosis Award for it; the profile describes the finished building but gives no completion date

details.text: Financing of Building 102: the terms also provide developer equity up to $14 million plus loans, and Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return.

open_questions: Current tenant: the Port's January 2019 memo gives the start of JUUL's ten-year sublease as 'TBD (upon completion of rehabilitation work)'; none of the sources listed here, the latest dated November 2020, confirms JUUL is still in Building 102 or names a successor.
Completion / certificate of occupancy date: the Port anticipated 2019; the November 2020 profile describes the finished building without a date.

The square-footage figures differ by source (8,428 NRHP vs 11,266 Port pre-rehab vs 15,500 magazine). The NRHP says its figure covers 'the first floor and basement', so the basement does not explain the gap, and the sources read do not say what each figure measures.

Construction start: the Port's January 2019 memo says construction followed the July 2015 execution of the master lease, the National Trust (Winter 2016 issue) says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' (the year is not printed), and Bisnow (April 2017) says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'. No source read settles the start year.
Size of Building 102 after rehabilitation: the Port's 2019 Table 1 gives 11,266 sq ft before and 15,331 after rehabilitation; Retrofit magazine gives 15,500 original and just over 18,000 after.

Public access to Building 102: the Port's January 2019 memo lists 'Building 102 key historic features' among 'spaces now open to the public (and to be open when construction is complete)'; the building was still under construction then, the memo does not say which listed spaces were already open, and no later source confirms public access.
